single_ablation.conclusion: The cross-sectional factor was not the terminal bottleneck. Removing it increased intermediate states but produced no complete trade because no retest carried material state-interval OI creation.

failure_classification.dominant_failure: The new-inventory continuation mechanism did not occur. Common-market acceptance and independent retests were observable, but raw exchange open interest never expanded sufficiently from before the sweep through the later retest.

valid_components_preserved: past-only cross-sectional median return and executed-flow factor
two completed outside closes plus index-proxy confirmation
next_hypothesis: Accepted external-liquidity sweeps accompanied by material OI contraction are forced-deleveraging continuation states. Continuation should require common-factor acceptance, price displacement despite OI destruction, a later held retest, no material OI rebuild, and common-factor resumption.
